title: [11/12/2021] - Oil production capacity for several Gulf countries between 1990 and 2010
prompt: The graph shows oil production capacity for several Gulf countries between 1990 and 2010. Summarize the key information by highlighting the main features and make appropriate comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The given bar chart compares the oil production capacity of six Middle Eastern countries in 1990, 2000, 2005, and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, it is clear that, with the exception of Qatar, all the countries shown expanded their capacity over the years, with Saudi Arabia being the largest producer, while Qatar was at the other end of the spectrum.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the countries that produced the most oil in the region, Saudi Arabia delivered exactly 8 million barrels a day in 1990, and this figure rose moderately over the next 10 years, before surging in the last decade to 14 million in 2010. Iran was the second largest producer; however, in contrast, its numbers were relatively more stable. They started the period at around 3 million barrels per day, and then production rose slightly and plateaued at around 4 million from 2000 to 2010.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: The next largest producers, namely Iraq, Kuwait and the UAE grew similarly, as their all production capacity started at around 2 million barrels a day in the first year, increasing steadily over the next 20 years and ending up approximately twice as high in 2010. Finally, Qatar’s numbers were insignificant and remained at around 0.5 million throughout the period shown.
